text.p: - Slovenian prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek is expected to present his new government line-up on Monday. Parliament is expected to vote on the proposal on February 27.
- Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats and conservative People's Party formed a coalition together with Desus, the pensioners' party, on Sunday.
- Slovenia's December investments rose 23.6 percent to 32.9 billion tolars ($215 million) compared to November and 72.4 percent compared to December 1995.
- Krka health resorts operator announced it will invest some $6.7 million over the next two years in modernising its facilities.
- The number of over-night stays in Slovenia in 1996 fell 0.9 percent to 5.8 million, compared to the 1995, the statistical office reported.
- The amount of money payed for child-support in 1996 rose by 27 percent to 40.2 billion tolars ($297.8 million), the ministry of labour said.
- The employment board of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) will hold a meeting in Ljubljana on Monday, this will be the OECD's first meeting in Slovenia.
- Slovenia's Celje qualified for the semifinals of the European handball Champions' league after beating Switzerland's Pfadi Winterthur 28-19 on Sunday.
